## DOMAINS

### Aesthetics and Philosophy of Art

Groups: 3 · Skills: 11

[aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Aesthetic inquiry asks why experiences, works, and environments are judged beautiful, expressive, meaningful, or artistically valuable. Its focus is justification and concepts of value, not techniques of making art.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why people consider experiences and artworks beautiful or valuable.

#### Aesthetic Judgment

Skills: 4

[aestheticJudgment.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt/aestheticJudgment/aestheticJudgment.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** An aesthetic evaluation can invoke perceptual qualities, interpretation, tradition, or standards that other observers may dispute.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how aesthetic opinions can be supported by reasons.

##### Analyze the role of context in aesthetic experience

[analyzeTheRoleOfContextInAestheticExperience.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt/aestheticJudgment/skills/analyzeTheRoleOfContextInAestheticExperience.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how setting, background knowledge, and cultural conventions can alter interpretation while the object remains unchanged.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how context or background knowledge changes an aesthetic experience.

##### Compare objective and subjective accounts of beauty

[compareObjectiveAndSubjectiveAccountsOfBeauty.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt/aestheticJudgment/skills/compareObjectiveAndSubjectiveAccountsOfBeauty.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Examine whether aesthetic assessments can be reasoned about beyond individual preference without assuming universal consensus.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare views about whether beauty can be judged beyond individual preference.

##### Distinguish aesthetic from instrumental value

[distinguishAestheticFromInstrumentalValue.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt/aestheticJudgment/skills/distinguishAestheticFromInstrumentalValue.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why something may be appreciated for its appearance or experience rather than its practical usefulness.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish an object's beauty or expressive value from its practical use.

##### Justify an aesthetic judgment

[justifyAnAestheticJudgment.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt/aestheticJudgment/skills/justifyAnAestheticJudgment.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Support an appraisal with relevant features and criteria rather than simply reporting that one likes or dislikes an object.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain an aesthetic evaluation using relevant features instead of personal taste alone.

#### Art and Interpretation

Skills: 4

[artAndInterpretation.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt/artAndInterpretation/artAndInterpretation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A work can bear meanings and values that are not reducible to the creator's stated intent or a viewer's immediate reaction.

**User-friendly description (en):** Consider how artworks can communicate meanings beyond what their makers intended.

##### Analyze the ethical evaluation of art

[analyzeTheEthicalEvaluationOfArt.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt/artAndInterpretation/skills/analyzeTheEthicalEvaluationOfArt.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explore whether and how moral concerns about content, production, or reception bear on artistic appraisal.

**User-friendly description (en):** Examine whether moral concerns should influence artistic judgment.

##### Compare interpretations of an artwork

[compareInterpretationsOfAnArtwork.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt/artAndInterpretation/skills/compareInterpretationsOfAnArtwork.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Evaluate rival readings by their attention to the work's features and context rather than assuming every reading is equally supported.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare interpretations of an artwork using evidence from its features and history.

##### Distinguish artistic intention from interpretation

[distinguishArtisticIntentionFromInterpretation.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt/artAndInterpretation/skills/distinguishArtisticIntentionFromInterpretation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assess what a creator reportedly intended separately from meanings supported by the work and its reception.

**User-friendly description (en):** Separate an artist's intentions from interpretations supported by the work.

##### Evaluate a definition of art

[evaluateADefinitionOfArt.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt/artAndInterpretation/skills/evaluateADefinitionOfArt.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Test a proposed criterion against borderline cases, changing practices, and works that challenge established categories.

**User-friendly description (en):** Test definitions of art against unusual or borderline examples.

#### Value and Taste

Skills: 3

[valueAndTaste.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt/valueAndTaste/valueAndTaste.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Debates about taste raise questions about expertise, social convention, and the relation of appreciation to human flourishing.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how personal taste, expertise and cultural traditions influence appreciation.

##### Analyze aesthetic pluralism

[analyzeAestheticPluralism.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt/valueAndTaste/skills/analyzeAestheticPluralism.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Examine how multiple traditions can sustain meaningful standards without requiring one global ranking of their forms.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how different artistic traditions can have meaningful standards of value.

##### Distinguish taste from an argued evaluation

[distinguishTasteFromAnArguedEvaluation.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt/valueAndTaste/skills/distinguishTasteFromAnArguedEvaluation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize that a personal reaction and a defensible public judgment may overlap but require different kinds of support.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize the difference between liking something and defending an evaluation of it.

##### Evaluate the role of expertise in aesthetic judgment

[evaluateTheRoleOfExpertiseInAestheticJudgment.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/aestheticsAndPhilosophyOfArt/valueAndTaste/skills/evaluateTheRoleOfExpertiseInAestheticJudgment.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Consider how practiced perception and historical knowledge may inform an assessment without making expert preferences infallible.

**User-friendly description (en):** Consider how expertise informs judgments without making experts infallible.

### Epistemology and Critical Evaluation

Groups: 4 · Skills: 19

[epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Questions about knowledge concern what can be believed responsibly, what makes claims true, and when confidence should change. This domain applies general standards of justification to testimony and public information; scientific experimental design has its own domain.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore what makes a belief justified and how to evaluate public information.

#### Evidence and Testimony

Skills: 5

[evidenceAndTestimony.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/evidenceAndTestimony/evidenceAndTestimony.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Knowledge often depends on information supplied by other people or institutions. Source reliability, independence, and evidential fit require appraisal without treating every source as equally trustworthy.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn to assess claims and evidence passed on by other people.

##### Analyze epistemic injustice

[analyzeEpistemicInjustice.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/evidenceAndTestimony/skills/analyzeEpistemicInjustice.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Examine how prejudicial credibility judgments or unequal interpretive resources can wrong someone in their capacity as a knower, distinct from warranted critical assessment of testimony.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how unfair judgments about credibility can prevent people from being heard.

##### Check corroboration across sources

[checkCorroborationAcrossSources.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/evidenceAndTestimony/skills/checkCorroborationAcrossSources.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine whether apparently agreeing accounts are genuinely independent or reproduce one underlying report.

**User-friendly description (en):** Check whether several agreeing sources truly provide independent evidence.

##### Distinguish a claim from its evidence

[distinguishAClaimFromItsEvidence.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/evidenceAndTestimony/skills/distinguishAClaimFromItsEvidence.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Separate what someone asserts from the observations, documents, or arguments presented to support it.

**User-friendly description (en):** Separate an assertion from the evidence used to support it.

##### Distinguish direct evidence from hearsay

[distinguishDirectEvidenceFromHearsay.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/evidenceAndTestimony/skills/distinguishDirectEvidenceFromHearsay.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize what a record or witness directly establishes and what depends on another person's retelling.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish firsthand records from claims repeated through others.

##### Evaluate testimonial credibility

[evaluateTestimonialCredibility.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/evidenceAndTestimony/skills/evaluateTestimonialCredibility.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Consider the speaker's opportunity to know, relevant competence, track record, and possible conflicts without reducing evaluation to popularity.

**User-friendly description (en):** Evaluate a witness or expert using relevant experience and possible conflicts.

#### Knowledge and Justification

Skills: 5

[knowledgeAndJustification.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/knowledgeAndJustification/knowledgeAndJustification.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Belief, truth, evidence, and knowledge have distinct roles in epistemic evaluation. Competing theories of knowledge can disagree about exactly how those roles connect.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how belief, truth, evidence and knowledge relate but differ.

##### Analyze mathematical proof as justification

[analyzeMathematicalProofAsJustification.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/knowledgeAndJustification/skills/analyzeMathematicalProofAsJustification.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Examine why deductive proof has a distinctive epistemic role in mathematics, distinguishing formal derivability from experimental confirmation and acknowledging debates about proof's explanatory value.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why mathematical proof differs from evidence gathered through experiments.

##### Compare a priori and empirical justification

[compareAPrioriAndEmpiricalJustification.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/knowledgeAndJustification/skills/compareAPrioriAndEmpiricalJustification.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish support based primarily on reasoning from support requiring experience, without assuming the boundary is universally uncontested.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare knowledge grounded in reasoning with knowledge grounded in experience.

##### Distinguish belief from knowledge

[distinguishBeliefFromKnowledge.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/knowledgeAndJustification/skills/distinguishBeliefFromKnowledge.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize that sincerely accepting a proposition does not by itself establish that it is known, even when the speaker is confident.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand why believing a claim sincerely does not automatically make it knowledge.

##### Distinguish truth from justification

[distinguishTruthFromJustification.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/knowledgeAndJustification/skills/distinguishTruthFromJustification.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why a claim might be true for reasons its holder cannot supply, or well supported yet ultimately false.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish a claim being true from having good reasons to believe it.

##### Evaluate reasons for a belief

[evaluateReasonsForABelief.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/knowledgeAndJustification/skills/evaluateReasonsForABelief.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine whether offered grounds actually bear on the proposition and withstand plausible objections.

**User-friendly description (en):** Check whether the reasons offered actually support a belief.

#### Media and Public Information

Skills: 5

[mediaAndPublicInformation.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/mediaAndPublicInformation/mediaAndPublicInformation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Information environments combine reporting, interpretation, promotion, and falsehood. Epistemic evaluation concerns the warrant for public claims, not the psychological mechanics by which messages persuade audiences.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn to investigate reporting, opinions and claims shared in public.

##### Distinguish misinformation from deliberate deception claims

[distinguishMisinformationFromDeliberateDeceptionClaims.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/mediaAndPublicInformation/skills/distinguishMisinformationFromDeliberateDeceptionClaims.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify inaccurate information without asserting an author's intention to deceive unless independent evidence supports that inference.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify inaccurate claims without assuming a speaker intended to deceive.

##### Distinguish reporting from opinion

[distinguishReportingFromOpinion.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/mediaAndPublicInformation/skills/distinguishReportingFromOpinion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify whether a passage presents checkable occurrences, interpretation, advocacy, or a mixture requiring separate evaluation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish factual reporting from interpretation and advocacy.

##### Evaluate evidence behind a headline

[evaluateEvidenceBehindAHeadline.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/mediaAndPublicInformation/skills/evaluateEvidenceBehindAHeadline.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare a summary with the underlying article or evidence and identify claims that exceed what is documented.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare a headline's promise with evidence provided in the underlying report.

##### Recognize misleading context in presented evidence

[recognizeMisleadingContextInPresentedEvidence.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/mediaAndPublicInformation/skills/recognizeMisleadingContextInPresentedEvidence.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Detect how cropping, omitted baselines, selective examples, or missing dates can alter the apparent meaning of otherwise genuine material.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how omitted dates, cropped images or missing context can mislead.

##### Trace a public claim to its original source

[traceAPublicClaimToItsOriginalSource.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/mediaAndPublicInformation/skills/traceAPublicClaimToItsOriginalSource.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Follow citations or reposts to determine what a primary document, recording, or dataset actually says.

**User-friendly description (en):** Follow a claim back to what its original document or recording actually says.

#### Uncertainty and Skepticism

Skills: 4

[uncertaintyAndSkepticism.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/uncertaintyAndSkepticism/uncertaintyAndSkepticism.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Rational inquiry must accommodate incomplete evidence and the possibility of error without collapsing into indiscriminate doubt.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how to think responsibly when evidence is incomplete.

##### Calibrate confidence to evidence

[calibrateConfidenceToEvidence.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/uncertaintyAndSkepticism/skills/calibrateConfidenceToEvidence.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Express degrees of certainty proportionate to the support available and identify what new information could change them.

**User-friendly description (en):** Adjust how certain you feel about a claim to match the available evidence.

##### Evaluate a skeptical challenge

[evaluateASkepticalChallenge.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/uncertaintyAndSkepticism/skills/evaluateASkepticalChallenge.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assess whether a proposed possibility of error undermines a specific knowledge claim or sets an unrealistically absolute standard.

**User-friendly description (en):** Evaluate whether a skeptical objection genuinely challenges a particular claim.

##### Identify a disagreement about evidence standards

[identifyADisagreementAboutEvidenceStandards.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/uncertaintyAndSkepticism/skills/identifyADisagreementAboutEvidenceStandards.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish people contesting a factual premise from people applying different thresholds for accepting the same evidence.

**User-friendly description (en):** Spot disagreements about the standard of evidence, not only the facts.

##### Recognize the limits of personal knowledge

[recognizeTheLimitsOfPersonalKnowledge.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/epistemologyAndCriticalEvaluation/uncertaintyAndSkepticism/skills/recognizeTheLimitsOfPersonalKnowledge.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Differentiate what one has observed, inferred, learned from others, or cannot currently establish.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize the difference between what you observed and what you only inferred.

### Ethics and Moral Reasoning

Groups: 5 · Skills: 25

[ethicsAndMoralReasoning.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/ethicsAndMoralReasoning.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Ethics studies what ought to be done, what makes actions right or wrong, and how moral reasons apply to individuals and institutions. It evaluates normative standards rather than describing the psychological development of moral feelings.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore what makes actions right or wrong and how to justify moral judgments.

#### Applied Ethics

Skills: 5

[appliedEthics.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/appliedEthics/appliedEthics.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Ethical principles face distinctive challenges when rights, vulnerable people, nonhuman life, and emerging technologies are involved.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore ethical questions about consent, privacy, animals, nature and technology.

##### Evaluate consent in an ethical scenario

[evaluateConsentInAnEthicalScenario.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/appliedEthics/skills/evaluateConsentInAnEthicalScenario.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assess whether a decision is adequately informed, voluntary, and within the decision-maker's authority.

**User-friendly description (en):** Check whether consent is informed, voluntary and given by the right person.

##### Evaluate duties toward nonhuman animals

[evaluateDutiesTowardNonhumanAnimals.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/appliedEthics/skills/evaluateDutiesTowardNonhumanAnimals.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare grounds for considering animal welfare or moral status in choices that affect sentient beings.

**User-friendly description (en):** Examine moral reasons for considering the welfare of nonhuman animals.

##### Evaluate environmental obligations

[evaluateEnvironmentalObligations.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/appliedEthics/skills/evaluateEnvironmentalObligations.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Examine duties to ecosystems and future generations, including trade-offs between present and long-term interests.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore obligations to ecosystems and future generations.

##### Evaluate ethical implications of automated decisions

[evaluateEthicalImplicationsOfAutomatedDecisions.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/appliedEthics/skills/evaluateEthicalImplicationsOfAutomatedDecisions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assess responsibility, contestability, fairness, and potential harm when an algorithm influences consequential choices.

**User-friendly description (en):** Evaluate fairness, accountability and harm in decisions influenced by algorithms.

##### Evaluate privacy as an ethical value

[evaluatePrivacyAsAnEthicalValue.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/appliedEthics/skills/evaluatePrivacyAsAnEthicalValue.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Reason about informational control, trust, and harms of disclosure beyond compliance with a particular law.

**User-friendly description (en):** Consider why privacy matters even beyond legal requirements.

#### Ethical Frameworks

Skills: 5

[ethicalFrameworks.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/ethicalFrameworks/ethicalFrameworks.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Normative theories emphasize different criteria of moral assessment. A theory is not a universal formula that automatically resolves every difficult case.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare major theories for evaluating right and wrong actions.

##### Apply care-ethical reasoning

[applyCareEthicalReasoning.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/ethicalFrameworks/skills/applyCareEthicalReasoning.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Evaluate obligations arising from dependence, relationships, vulnerability, and context without treating care as the absence of principles.

**User-friendly description (en):** Consider vulnerability, relationships and care when evaluating obligations.

##### Apply consequentialist reasoning

[applyConsequentialistReasoning.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/ethicalFrameworks/skills/applyConsequentialistReasoning.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Evaluate an action by outcomes and the welfare or values its consequences affect, accounting for affected parties.

**User-friendly description (en):** Consider likely outcomes and everyone affected when evaluating a choice.

##### Apply duty-based reasoning

[applyDutyBasedReasoning.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/ethicalFrameworks/skills/applyDutyBasedReasoning.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assess whether an act respects a rule, obligation, or person's standing even when violating it might have beneficial effects.

**User-friendly description (en):** Judge an action in light of duties and rights as well as its consequences.

##### Apply virtue-ethical reasoning

[applyVirtueEthicalReasoning.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/ethicalFrameworks/skills/applyVirtueEthicalReasoning.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Consider the traits and practical judgment exemplified by an action rather than evaluating only isolated rules or outcomes.

**User-friendly description (en):** Ask what an action shows about character and practical wisdom.

##### Compare ethical frameworks on one dilemma

[compareEthicalFrameworksOnOneDilemma.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/ethicalFrameworks/skills/compareEthicalFrameworksOnOneDilemma.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why distinct normative standards may support different recommendations even when the underlying facts are shared.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare how different moral theories reach conclusions about one dilemma.

#### Metaethics

Skills: 6

[metaethics.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/metaethics/metaethics.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Inquiry into the meaning, objectivity, and epistemic standing of moral discourse underlies but does not itself prescribe codes of conduct. Normative theories decide how to act; metaethical theories examine the status of such judgments.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore what moral claims mean and whether moral truths depend on personal beliefs.

##### Analyze moral disagreement

[analyzeMoralDisagreement.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/metaethics/skills/analyzeMoralDisagreement.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify whether disputants differ about facts, principles, or the status of moral claims, and what kinds of reasons could address those differences.

**User-friendly description (en):** Separate disagreements over facts from disagreements over moral standards.

##### Compare moral realism and anti-realism

[compareMoralRealismAndAntiRealism.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/metaethics/skills/compareMoralRealismAndAntiRealism.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assess opposing views about whether moral truths exist independently of attitudes, and distinguish this ontological disagreement from practical moral choices.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare views that affirm objective moral truths with views that reject them.

##### Distinguish metaethical from normative questions

[distinguishMetaethicalFromNormativeQuestions.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/metaethics/skills/distinguishMetaethicalFromNormativeQuestions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Separate questions about which actions are right from questions about what moral claims mean and whether their truth is objective.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish asking what is right from asking what moral judgments mean.

##### Distinguish moral cognitivism from non-cognitivism

[distinguishMoralCognitivismFromNonCognitivism.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/metaethics/skills/distinguishMoralCognitivismFromNonCognitivism.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Examine whether moral utterances express truth-apt beliefs or instead function as prescriptions, commitments, or other attitudes.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore whether moral sentences state facts or express attitudes and commitments.

##### Evaluate moral relativism

[evaluateMoralRelativism.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/metaethics/skills/evaluateMoralRelativism.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Test the view that moral truth or justification varies by culture or individual against cases involving disagreement, criticism, and reform.

**User-friendly description (en):** Examine whether right and wrong depend on culture or individual perspective.

##### Examine moral motivation

[examineMoralMotivation.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/metaethics/skills/examineMoralMotivation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare philosophical positions on whether sincerely judging an act right necessarily motivates someone to perform it, without substituting a psychological causal theory.

**User-friendly description (en):** Consider whether believing something is right necessarily motivates action.

#### Moral Concepts

Skills: 4

[moralConcepts.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/moralConcepts/moralConcepts.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Ethical claims use concepts such as duty, harm, intention, and virtue that cannot be reduced to personal approval.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn to recognize concepts such as duty, intention, harm and moral responsibility.

##### Analyze moral duty

[analyzeMoralDuty.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/moralConcepts/skills/analyzeMoralDuty.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify what it means to hold that a person is obligated to act even when doing so is inconvenient.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand why moral obligations can apply even when fulfilling them is inconvenient.

##### Distinguish intentions from consequences

[distinguishIntentionsFromConsequences.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/moralConcepts/skills/distinguishIntentionsFromConsequences.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why an action's aim and its actual effects may be evaluated separately in moral reasoning.

**User-friendly description (en):** Evaluate an action's intended purpose separately from its effects.

##### Distinguish moral from non-moral judgments

[distinguishMoralFromNonMoralJudgments.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/moralConcepts/skills/distinguishMoralFromNonMoralJudgments.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify when a claim concerns obligations or rights rather than taste, etiquette, prudence, or mere legality.

**User-friendly description (en):** Tell ethical claims apart from personal taste, etiquette and legal rules.

##### Distinguish moral responsibility from causal responsibility

[distinguishMoralResponsibilityFromCausalResponsibility.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/moralConcepts/skills/distinguishMoralResponsibilityFromCausalResponsibility.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Separate causing an outcome from being appropriately accountable for it under relevant knowledge and control conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish responsibility for causing something from deserving moral blame.

#### Moral Deliberation

Skills: 5

[moralDeliberation.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/moralDeliberation/moralDeliberation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Difficult cases require identifying who is affected, which reasons conflict, and whether an apparent compromise respects relevant obligations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn to reason through difficult choices with competing ethical considerations.

##### Assess proportionality in moral decisions

[assessProportionalityInMoralDecisions.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/moralDeliberation/skills/assessProportionalityInMoralDecisions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Consider whether a harmful burden or restriction is justified in relation to its aim and less harmful alternatives.

**User-friendly description (en):** Evaluate whether harms or restrictions are proportionate to a justified aim.

##### Evaluate a moral counterargument

[evaluateAMoralCounterargument.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/moralDeliberation/skills/evaluateAMoralCounterargument.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Test whether an objection exposes an overlooked harm, inconsistency, or relevant exception to a principle.

**User-friendly description (en):** Consider objections that reveal harms, exceptions or inconsistencies.

##### Identify conflicting moral obligations

[identifyConflictingMoralObligations.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/moralDeliberation/skills/identifyConflictingMoralObligations.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Specify duties or values that cannot all be fully honored in a concrete case without assuming that all conflicts are irresolvable.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when two ethical obligations cannot both be fully honored.

##### Identify stakeholders in an ethical dilemma

[identifyStakeholdersInAnEthicalDilemma.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/moralDeliberation/skills/identifyStakeholdersInAnEthicalDilemma.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize persons or other morally relevant parties affected directly or indirectly by a proposed choice.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify all the people and other parties affected by a moral choice.

##### Justify a moral judgment

[justifyAMoralJudgment.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/ethicsAndMoralReasoning/moralDeliberation/skills/justifyAMoralJudgment.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Connect a normative conclusion to stated values, principles, and case facts rather than mere personal preference.

**User-friendly description (en):** Support a moral judgment using explicit principles and relevant facts.

### History and Traditions of Philosophy

Groups: 3 · Skills: 15

[historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Historically situated philosophical arguments develop through schools, intellectual movements, and traditions across cultures. Interpretation requires understanding both what a thinker argued and the debate that shaped the argument, without privileging one lineage as philosophy's default.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore philosophical ideas across cultures and historical periods through their arguments.

#### Philosophical Traditions

Skills: 8

[philosophicalTraditions.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/philosophicalTraditions/philosophicalTraditions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Intellectual traditions developed across many cultures through original arguments and sustained exchanges. Greek, Indian, Chinese, Islamic, African, Latin American, and particular Indigenous lineages are examined as philosophical sources in their own right, without treating a region as a single doctrine.

**User-friendly description (en):** Examine philosophical arguments developed in many distinct cultural traditions.

##### Analyze a philosophical argument from a Chinese tradition

[analyzeAPhilosophicalArgumentFromAChineseTradition.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/philosophicalTraditions/skills/analyzeAPhilosophicalArgumentFromAChineseTradition.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret a position in a specific Chinese philosophical lineage, such as Confucian or Daoist thinking, without conflating them.

**User-friendly description (en):** Interpret a philosophical claim from a Chinese tradition in its proper context.

##### Analyze a philosophical argument from a Latin American tradition

[analyzeAPhilosophicalArgumentFromALatinAmericanTradition.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/philosophicalTraditions/skills/analyzeAPhilosophicalArgumentFromALatinAmericanTradition.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Reconstruct an argument from a specific Latin American current, such as liberation or decolonial philosophy, in its intellectual and social context without reducing the region to one doctrine.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore Latin American philosophical arguments in their social and intellectual context.

##### Analyze a philosophical argument from an African tradition

[analyzeAPhilosophicalArgumentFromAnAfricanTradition.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/philosophicalTraditions/skills/analyzeAPhilosophicalArgumentFromAnAfricanTradition.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Examine a representative argument concerning persons, community, knowledge, or values while avoiding claims that Africa has a single philosophy.

**User-friendly description (en):** Analyze a philosophical argument from a particular African tradition.

##### Analyze a philosophical argument from an Indian tradition

[analyzeAPhilosophicalArgumentFromAnIndianTradition.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/philosophicalTraditions/skills/analyzeAPhilosophicalArgumentFromAnIndianTradition.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify claims and reasons in a specific Indian philosophical school while preserving its distinctive terms and internal disagreements.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore an argument from a specific Indian philosophical school.

##### Analyze a philosophical argument from an Indigenous tradition

[analyzeAPhilosophicalArgumentFromAnIndigenousTradition.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/philosophicalTraditions/skills/analyzeAPhilosophicalArgumentFromAnIndigenousTradition.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret philosophical claims from a particular Indigenous people or intellectual tradition on their own conceptual terms, recognizing differences among communities and avoiding a generic 'Indigenous worldview'.

**User-friendly description (en):** Consider philosophical ideas from a particular Indigenous tradition on its own terms.

##### Analyze a philosophical argument from an Islamic tradition

[analyzeAPhilosophicalArgumentFromAnIslamicTradition.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/philosophicalTraditions/skills/analyzeAPhilosophicalArgumentFromAnIslamicTradition.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain a selected debate in Islamic philosophy using its intellectual context rather than assuming theology and philosophy are identical.

**User-friendly description (en):** Examine a debate within Islamic philosophy using its historical setting.

##### Compare classical Greek philosophical approaches

[compareClassicalGreekPhilosophicalApproaches.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/philosophicalTraditions/skills/compareClassicalGreekPhilosophicalApproaches.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Contrast representative methods or commitments in Socratic, Platonic, and Aristotelian arguments without collapsing them into one doctrine.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare ideas associated with Socrates, Plato and Aristotle.

##### Compare positions across philosophical traditions

[comparePositionsAcrossPhilosophicalTraditions.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/philosophicalTraditions/skills/comparePositionsAcrossPhilosophicalTraditions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify a genuine shared problem and meaningful conceptual differences without forcing one tradition's categories onto another.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare how different traditions address similar philosophical questions.

#### Reading Philosophical Works

Skills: 4

[readingPhilosophicalWorks.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/readingPhilosophicalWorks/readingPhilosophicalWorks.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Texts require interpreting claims, their argumentative context, and the questions the author sought to answer; historical wording cannot always be mapped directly to modern categories.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn to read philosophical works with attention to their questions and context.

##### Evaluate a philosophical text critically

[evaluateAPhilosophicalTextCritically.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/readingPhilosophicalWorks/skills/evaluateAPhilosophicalTextCritically.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assess reasons offered in a source rather than accepting or rejecting a view solely because of the author's reputation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Evaluate the reasons in a classic philosophical text, not just its author's reputation.

##### Identify the central problem in a philosophical text

[identifyTheCentralProblemInAPhilosophicalText.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/readingPhilosophicalWorks/skills/identifyTheCentralProblemInAPhilosophicalText.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine which issue motivates an argument rather than treating every illustrative passage as the main thesis.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify the main problem a philosopher is trying to address.

##### Interpret a philosopher in historical context

[interpretAPhilosopherInHistoricalContext.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/readingPhilosophicalWorks/skills/interpretAPhilosopherInHistoricalContext.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use contemporaneous debates and available concepts to avoid attributing later assumptions to an earlier author.

**User-friendly description (en):** Interpret philosophical views in light of the debates of their own time.

##### Reconstruct a historical philosophical argument

[reconstructAHistoricalPhilosophicalArgument.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/readingPhilosophicalWorks/skills/reconstructAHistoricalPhilosophicalArgument.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Extract claims and reasons from a source while distinguishing a philosopher's stated position from later summaries.

**User-friendly description (en):** Reconstruct a historical argument using what the philosopher actually wrote.

#### Schools and Movements

Skills: 3

[schoolsAndMovements.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/schoolsAndMovements/schoolsAndMovements.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Philosophical movements and schools arise around distinctive approaches to knowledge, reason, liberty, and existence; their boundaries and internal disagreements cannot be reduced to dates alone.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how different philosophical schools approach shared questions.

##### Analyze an Enlightenment philosophical argument

[analyzeAnEnlightenmentPhilosophicalArgument.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/schoolsAndMovements/skills/analyzeAnEnlightenmentPhilosophicalArgument.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Place a claim about reason, liberty, or authority in its intellectual context while acknowledging diverse and conflicting Enlightenment positions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore Enlightenment arguments about reason, authority and freedom.

##### Compare existentialist and analytic approaches to a problem

[compareExistentialistAndAnalyticApproachesToAProblem.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/schoolsAndMovements/skills/compareExistentialistAndAnalyticApproachesToAProblem.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify differences in methods and questions without claiming that either broad family has one uniform answer.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare existentialist and analytic approaches without oversimplifying either tradition.

##### Compare major modern epistemological approaches

[compareMajorModernEpistemologicalApproaches.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/historyAndTraditionsOfPhilosophy/schoolsAndMovements/skills/compareMajorModernEpistemologicalApproaches.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the distinct emphases of rationalist, empiricist, and critical traditions through representative arguments.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare how rationalism, empiricism and critical philosophy approach knowledge.

### Logic and Argumentation

Groups: 6 · Skills: 35

[logicAndArgumentation.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/logicAndArgumentation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The central question is whether reasons support a conclusion and in what way. Formal entailment, defeasible inference, and argumentative defects are distinguished from psychological causes of belief, which belong chiefly to Psychology.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn to evaluate whether reasons support a conclusion and recognize faulty reasoning.

#### Argumentative Fallacies

Skills: 6

[argumentativeFallacies.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/argumentativeFallacies/argumentativeFallacies.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A flaw concerns the relation between claims and reasons, not necessarily the speaker's motives or a named cognitive bias. Context matters: surface wording alone rarely proves fallaciousness.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn to recognize common flaws in the support offered for claims.

##### Detect a false dilemma

[detectAFalseDilemma.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/argumentativeFallacies/skills/detectAFalseDilemma.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify a purported exhaustive choice that overlooks meaningful alternatives or combined possibilities.

**User-friendly description (en):** Find meaningful alternatives hidden by a misleading either-or choice.

##### Detect a straw-man argument

[detectAStrawManArgument.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/argumentativeFallacies/skills/detectAStrawManArgument.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Show where a position is distorted into an easier target and recover the actual view before evaluating it.

**User-friendly description (en):** Notice when someone's position is distorted into an easier argument to attack.

##### Detect an ad hominem fallacy

[detectAnAdHominemFallacy.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/argumentativeFallacies/skills/detectAnAdHominemFallacy.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify when a personal attack substitutes for addressing reasons, while distinguishing relevant credibility evidence from irrelevant insults.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when a personal attack replaces relevant reasoning.

##### Detect an equivocation fallacy

[detectAnEquivocationFallacy.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/argumentativeFallacies/skills/detectAnEquivocationFallacy.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Trace a shift between meanings of the same expression that makes an inference appear stronger than it is.

**User-friendly description (en):** Spot when the meaning of a word shifts within an argument.

##### Detect circular reasoning

[detectCircularReasoning.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/argumentativeFallacies/skills/detectCircularReasoning.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize when the offered support presupposes the very claim at issue without independent justification.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize arguments that assume the conclusion they claim to prove.

##### Evaluate an appeal to authority

[evaluateAnAppealToAuthority.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/argumentativeFallacies/skills/evaluateAnAppealToAuthority.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Examine whether expertise is relevant and reliable evidence in context, rather than assuming that invoking any authority proves a conclusion.

**User-friendly description (en):** Decide whether cited expertise is relevant evidence rather than automatic proof.

#### Arguments and Inference

Skills: 4

[argumentsAndInference.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/argumentsAndInference/argumentsAndInference.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Arguments connect propositions through an inferential claim; assertions, explanations, and rhetorical appeals may occur nearby without playing the same role.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how premises and conclusions form an argument.

##### Distinguish an argument from an explanation

[distinguishAnArgumentFromAnExplanation.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/argumentsAndInference/skills/distinguishAnArgumentFromAnExplanation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Tell reasoning intended to establish a claim from an account of why an already accepted event or fact occurred.

**User-friendly description (en):** Tell a reason for believing something apart from an explanation of an accepted fact.

##### Identify an argument's conclusion

[identifyAnArgumentsConclusion.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/argumentsAndInference/skills/identifyAnArgumentsConclusion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine which proposition is supposed to follow or gain support, regardless of its position in a passage.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify the central claim an argument is trying to establish.

##### Identify premises in an argument

[identifyPremisesInAnArgument.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/argumentsAndInference/skills/identifyPremisesInAnArgument.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Locate the reasons offered in support of a conclusion, including unstated propositions when context makes them indispensable.

**User-friendly description (en):** Find the statements offered as reasons for a claim.

##### Reconstruct an argument in standard form

[reconstructAnArgumentInStandardForm.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/argumentsAndInference/skills/reconstructAnArgumentInStandardForm.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Arrange its relevant premises and conclusion explicitly while preserving the original reasoning rather than improving it silently.

**User-friendly description (en):** Rewrite an argument as clear premises followed by its conclusion.

#### Deductive Reasoning

Skills: 6

[deductiveReasoning.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/deductiveReasoning/deductiveReasoning.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Deduction concerns whether it is possible for premises to be true while a conclusion is false. Logical form is evaluated separately from whether the premises describe the world correctly.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore when conclusions necessarily follow from given premises.

##### Apply modus ponens

[applyModusPonens.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/deductiveReasoning/skills/applyModusPonens.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Infer a consequent from a conditional and its antecedent without treating the inverse conditional as equivalent.

**User-friendly description (en):** Apply the rule that if A implies B and A holds, then B follows.

##### Apply modus tollens

[applyModusTollens.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/deductiveReasoning/skills/applyModusTollens.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Reject the antecedent of a conditional from the denial of its consequent, under the conditional as stated.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use a conditional and the denial of its result to reject its antecedent.

##### Assess deductive validity

[assessDeductiveValidity.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/deductiveReasoning/skills/assessDeductiveValidity.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine whether a conclusion must hold if the premises hold, using logical structure rather than agreement with the conclusion.

**User-friendly description (en):** Check whether premises could all be true while a conclusion is false.

##### Distinguish validity from soundness

[distinguishValidityFromSoundness.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/deductiveReasoning/skills/distinguishValidityFromSoundness.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize that a sound deductive argument requires both a valid inference and true premises.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand why a logically valid argument can still have false premises.

##### Evaluate a categorical syllogism

[evaluateACategoricalSyllogism.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/deductiveReasoning/skills/evaluateACategoricalSyllogism.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Examine whether relations among classes support the proposed conclusion, rather than relying on familiar subject matter.

**User-friendly description (en):** Determine whether statements about categories logically support a conclusion.

##### Identify a contradiction in a set of claims

[identifyAContradictionInASetOfClaims.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/deductiveReasoning/skills/identifyAContradictionInASetOfClaims.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Show where commitments cannot all be true together under the same meanings and conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize claims that cannot all be true under the same conditions.

#### Non-deductive Reasoning

Skills: 4

[nonDeductiveReasoning.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/nonDeductiveReasoning/nonDeductiveReasoning.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Many reasonable arguments support conclusions without guaranteeing them. Their strength depends on evidence, alternatives, sampling, or explanatory power rather than formal certainty.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn to assess reasoning that offers support without guaranteeing certainty.

##### Distinguish deductive certainty from probabilistic support

[distinguishDeductiveCertaintyFromProbabilisticSupport.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/nonDeductiveReasoning/skills/distinguishDeductiveCertaintyFromProbabilisticSupport.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize that a well-supported conclusion can remain revisable when the reasoning is non-deductive.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish logically certain deductions from conclusions supported by probability.

##### Evaluate an inductive generalization

[evaluateAnInductiveGeneralization.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/nonDeductiveReasoning/skills/evaluateAnInductiveGeneralization.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Judge how well observed cases support a claim about a broader population, including the relevance of selection and variation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Evaluate how well observed examples support a broader generalization.

##### Evaluate an inference to the best explanation

[evaluateAnInferenceToTheBestExplanation.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/nonDeductiveReasoning/skills/evaluateAnInferenceToTheBestExplanation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare hypotheses by how well they explain evidence, their assumptions, and their fit with alternative explanations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Choose between possible explanations using evidence and assumptions.

##### Evaluate analogical reasoning

[evaluateAnalogicalReasoning.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/nonDeductiveReasoning/skills/evaluateAnalogicalReasoning.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Check whether compared cases share features relevant to the proposed conclusion rather than merely superficial similarities.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare cases by similarities that actually matter to the conclusion.

#### Predicate Logic

Skills: 6

[predicateLogic.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/predicateLogic/predicateLogic.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Variables and quantifiers permit reasoning about individuals and collections. The relevant universe and scope of each quantifier must be made explicit to evaluate meaning and inference.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how quantifiers express claims about all or some members of a group.

##### Analyze the scope of a quantifier

[analyzeTheScopeOfAQuantifier.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/predicateLogic/skills/analyzeTheScopeOfAQuantifier.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify which variables and expressions are governed by a quantifier and how scope changes the meaning of a formula.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how the placement of a quantifier changes the meaning of a statement.

##### Distinguish predicates from propositions

[distinguishPredicatesFromPropositions.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/predicateLogic/skills/distinguishPredicatesFromPropositions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize a predicate with an unbound variable as an open expression and a proposition as a statement with specified truth conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish an open expression about a variable from a complete proposition.

##### Evaluate an inference with quantifiers

[evaluateAnInferenceWithQuantifiers.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/predicateLogic/skills/evaluateAnInferenceWithQuantifiers.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Check whether a conclusion about all or some members of a domain follows from quantified premises under a stated interpretation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Check whether quantified premises really imply a proposed conclusion.

##### Interpret existential quantification

[interpretExistentialQuantification.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/predicateLogic/skills/interpretExistentialQuantification.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine what it means for at least one element of a specified domain to satisfy a property, without implying uniqueness.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how 'there exists' means at least one matching example.

##### Interpret universal quantification

[interpretUniversalQuantification.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/predicateLogic/skills/interpretUniversalQuantification.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine what it means for a property to hold for every element of a specified domain and how one counterexample would matter.

**User-friendly description (en):** Read a statement that applies to every member of a specified group.

##### Negate a quantified proposition

[negateAQuantifiedProposition.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/predicateLogic/skills/negateAQuantifiedProposition.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use the relationships between not-all and some-not, and between none and there-exists, to interpret negation accurately.

**User-friendly description (en):** Negate statements involving 'all' or 'some' without changing their meaning incorrectly.

#### Propositional Logic

Skills: 9

[propositionalLogic.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/propositionalLogic/propositionalLogic.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Truth-functional connections between propositions determine the logical properties of compound statements. Symbolic operators and truth tables clarify implications independent of the subject matter used in examples.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how truth conditions work for statements joined by logical operators.

##### Classify a proposition using a truth table

[classifyAPropositionUsingATruthTable.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/propositionalLogic/skills/classifyAPropositionUsingATruthTable.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish tautological, contradictory, and contingent expressions through their truth values under all assignments.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use truth tables to recognize always-true, always-false and contingent statements.

##### Construct a truth table

[constructATruthTable.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/propositionalLogic/skills/constructATruthTable.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Enumerate truth-value combinations for atomic propositions and systematically compute outcomes of logical expressions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Construct a table of possible truth assignments for a logical expression.

##### Distinguish atomic from compound propositions

[distinguishAtomicFromCompoundPropositions.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/propositionalLogic/skills/distinguishAtomicFromCompoundPropositions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A proposition can stand alone or form part of a statement built with logical connectives; truth-functional structure differs from the number of words in an ordinary sentence.

**User-friendly description (en):** Tell a single proposition apart from one assembled with logical connectives.

##### Interpret logical biconditional

[interpretLogicalBiconditional.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/propositionalLogic/skills/interpretLogicalBiconditional.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assess 'if and only if' statements as two-way conditional relationships, rather than treating either one-way conditional as sufficient.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize that 'if and only if' requires implications in both directions.

##### Interpret logical conjunction

[interpretLogicalConjunction.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/propositionalLogic/skills/interpretLogicalConjunction.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Apply the truth conditions of logical 'and' while distinguishing conjunction from a chronological or causal relationship.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when a logical AND statement is true.

##### Interpret logical disjunction

[interpretLogicalDisjunction.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/propositionalLogic/skills/interpretLogicalDisjunction.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Apply the truth conditions of inclusive 'or' and distinguish these from interpretations that require exactly one alternative.

**User-friendly description (en):** Interpret inclusive OR without assuming only one option can be true.

##### Interpret logical negation

[interpretLogicalNegation.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/propositionalLogic/skills/interpretLogicalNegation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine when the denial of a proposition is true and distinguish negation from a stronger contrary statement.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how negating a claim changes its truth conditions.

##### Interpret material implication

[interpretMaterialImplication.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/propositionalLogic/skills/interpretMaterialImplication.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine when a conditional is true in classical propositional logic without confusing logical implication with causation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand when a conditional is true in classical propositional logic.

##### Test deductive validity using a truth table

[testDeductiveValidityUsingATruthTable.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/logicAndArgumentation/propositionalLogic/skills/testDeductiveValidityUsingATruthTable.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Search for a case in which all premises are true but the conclusion false to determine propositional validity.

**User-friendly description (en):** Check a deduction by searching for true premises with a false conclusion.

### Metaphysics

Groups: 4 · Skills: 14

[metaphysics.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/metaphysics.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Metaphysics examines the most general categories of reality, such as what exists, how things persist, and what makes events possible. Its conceptual questions differ from describing particular natural mechanisms in the sciences.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore philosophical questions about existence, identity, reality, time and possibility.

#### Causation, Time, and Possibility

Skills: 4

[causationTimeAndPossibility.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/causationTimeAndPossibility/causationTimeAndPossibility.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Metaphysical inquiry asks what causal dependence means and how temporal or modal claims relate beyond specific measurements.

**User-friendly description (en):** Examine philosophical ideas about cause, time and what could have happened.

##### Compare philosophical accounts of time

[comparePhilosophicalAccountsOfTime.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/causationTimeAndPossibility/skills/comparePhilosophicalAccountsOfTime.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain differences between views that privilege the present and views treating past, present, and future as equally real.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare views about whether only the present or all times are equally real.

##### Distinguish causation from temporal succession

[distinguishCausationFromTemporalSuccession.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/causationTimeAndPossibility/skills/distinguishCausationFromTemporalSuccession.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize that one event occurring before another does not itself establish a productive or counterfactual dependence.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize why an earlier event is not necessarily the cause of a later one.

##### Distinguish possibility from necessity

[distinguishPossibilityFromNecessity.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/causationTimeAndPossibility/skills/distinguishPossibilityFromNecessity.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify claims that could be otherwise and those held to be true in every relevant possible circumstance.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish something that might happen from something that must be true.

##### Evaluate a counterfactual claim

[evaluateACounterfactualClaim.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/causationTimeAndPossibility/skills/evaluateACounterfactualClaim.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Examine what would follow if specified conditions had differed while keeping relevant background assumptions coherent.

**User-friendly description (en):** Assess what might follow under an imagined alternative set of conditions.

#### Existence and Categories

Skills: 3

[existenceAndCategories.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/existenceAndCategories/existenceAndCategories.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Different theories posit concrete objects, properties, events, or abstract entities; their classification determines what kinds of ontological commitments a claim makes.

**User-friendly description (en):** Examine different kinds of things that philosophers consider real.

##### Distinguish concrete from abstract entities

[distinguishConcreteFromAbstractEntities.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/existenceAndCategories/skills/distinguishConcreteFromAbstractEntities.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assess whether a proposed entity has spatial or causal features characteristic of concrete things or is treated as abstract, such as a mathematical object.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish physical objects from entities such as numbers or abstract ideas.

##### Distinguish properties from objects

[distinguishPropertiesFromObjects.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/existenceAndCategories/skills/distinguishPropertiesFromObjects.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Separate a bearer from qualities attributed to it, while recognizing that some metaphysical theories analyze this distinction differently.

**User-friendly description (en):** Separate an object from the properties attributed to it.

##### Evaluate an existence claim

[evaluateAnExistenceClaim.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/existenceAndCategories/skills/evaluateAnExistenceClaim.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Examine the criteria by which something is said to exist rather than assuming that naming it settles its ontological status.

**User-friendly description (en):** Ask what evidence or reasoning supports saying that something exists.

#### Identity and Persistence

Skills: 4

[identityAndPersistence.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/identityAndPersistence/identityAndPersistence.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Questions about sameness arise when material, properties, or relations change over time. Numerical identity is different from merely sharing characteristics.

**User-friendly description (en):** Ask what makes something remain the same thing through change.

##### Analyze a metaphysical paradox

[analyzeAMetaphysicalParadox.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/identityAndPersistence/skills/analyzeAMetaphysicalParadox.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify apparently plausible assumptions that generate inconsistent conclusions in a puzzle about reality.

**User-friendly description (en):** Uncover conflicting assumptions in puzzles about the nature of reality.

##### Analyze a part–whole relation

[analyzeAPartWholeRelation.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/identityAndPersistence/skills/analyzeAPartWholeRelation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Examine whether a component and a composite have different identities and what changes follow from replacing parts.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how an object's parts relate to the whole they compose.

##### Distinguish numerical from qualitative identity

[distinguishNumericalFromQualitativeIdentity.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/identityAndPersistence/skills/distinguishNumericalFromQualitativeIdentity.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify the difference between being one and the same entity and being indistinguishable in specified properties.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish being the same individual object from merely looking identical.

##### Evaluate persistence through change

[evaluatePersistenceThroughChange.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/identityAndPersistence/skills/evaluatePersistenceThroughChange.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assess competing criteria for when an object remains the same despite replacement, growth, or alteration.

**User-friendly description (en):** Consider whether replacing parts changes the identity of an object.

#### Mathematical Reality

Skills: 3

[mathematicalReality.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/mathematicalReality/mathematicalReality.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Philosophical accounts of mathematics disagree over whether its objects exist independently, are constructs of formal language, or are positions within structures. These ontological commitments are distinct from learning to perform mathematical operations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore debates about whether mathematical objects exist independently of people.

##### Analyze mathematical structuralism

[analyzeMathematicalStructuralism.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/mathematicalReality/skills/analyzeMathematicalStructuralism.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Evaluate the claim that mathematical objects are understood through positions and relations in structures rather than through individually identifying intrinsic properties.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore whether mathematical objects are best understood by their relationships.

##### Evaluate mathematical nominalism

[evaluateMathematicalNominalism.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/mathematicalReality/skills/evaluateMathematicalNominalism.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Examine strategies for understanding mathematical language and successful reasoning without committing to independently existing abstract mathematical objects.

**User-friendly description (en):** Evaluate how mathematical reasoning might work without independently existing abstract objects.

##### Evaluate mathematical Platonism

[evaluateMathematicalPlatonism.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/metaphysics/mathematicalReality/skills/evaluateMathematicalPlatonism.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assess the view that mathematical objects or structures exist independently of human thought and how it attempts to explain the apparent objectivity of mathematics.

**User-friendly description (en):** Examine arguments that mathematical entities exist independently of human minds.

### Mind, Self, and Human Existence

Groups: 4 · Skills: 17

[mindSelfAndHumanExistence.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/mindSelfAndHumanExistence/mindSelfAndHumanExistence.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Questions about subjective experience, the continuity of the self, deliberate action, and a meaningful human life cannot be resolved solely through psychological measurement. This domain examines theories of mind, identity, agency, and existential commitments, distinguishing them from empirical mental-health claims.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore philosophical questions about consciousness, personal identity, freedom and meaning.

#### Agency and Free Will

Skills: 5

[agencyAndFreeWill.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/mindSelfAndHumanExistence/agencyAndFreeWill/agencyAndFreeWill.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Acting for reasons, selecting among alternatives, and being accountable are connected but separable philosophical ideas.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how choice, reasons and responsibility relate to freedom.

##### Compare compatibilist and incompatibilist freedom

[compareCompatibilistAndIncompatibilistFreedom.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/mindSelfAndHumanExistence/agencyAndFreeWill/skills/compareCompatibilistAndIncompatibilistFreedom.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Examine whether meaningful free action is possible under determinism and how rival views define freedom.

**User-friendly description (en):** Examine whether freedom and responsibility can coexist with determinism.

##### Compare determinism and indeterminism

[compareDeterminismAndIndeterminism.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/mindSelfAndHumanExistence/agencyAndFreeWill/skills/compareDeterminismAndIndeterminism.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the different claims about how events are determined and why randomness alone does not establish control.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare a fully determined world with one that allows indeterminate events.

##### Distinguish an action from an event

[distinguishAnActionFromAnEvent.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/mindSelfAndHumanExistence/agencyAndFreeWill/skills/distinguishAnActionFromAnEvent.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify whether a description invokes an agent's intention or reason rather than only something that happened to a body.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish an intentional action from something that merely happens.

##### Distinguish reasons for action from causes of behavior

[distinguishReasonsForActionFromCausesOfBehavior.data.ts](../../../content/philosophy/data/skills/mindSelfAndHumanExistence/agencyAndFreeWill/skills/distinguishReasonsForActionFromCausesOfBehavior.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Separate justifying considerations from causal explanations, recognizing that the two may be related.
